title: Mitered Chevron Cutout Halter Top (Size S/M)
text:
This reproducible pattern generates a Women’s Size S/M 100% Cotton Mitered Chevron Halter Top calibrated for an ~88 cm bust / ~76 cm underbust (38.0 cm front panel baseline + 2 × 14.0 cm ribbed back extensions + 10.0 cm corset lace-up gap).
Unlike naive chevron patterns that assume square stitches, every stitch count, short-row turn, blueprint polygon, and yardage estimate on this page is computed dynamically in R from Euclidean trigonometry using the true aspect ratio of half double crochet (sts/cm != rows/cm). Edit any gauge or measurement variable in the setup chunk below and re-render with Quarto to recalibrate the entire pattern.

1. Parameterized R Setup & Trigonometric Stitch Engine


Show R setup & trigonometric stitch engine
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(knitr)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. TUNABLE GARMENT, YARN & GAUGE PARAMETERS
# ==============================================================================

# Yarn specifications: Sport weight (#2) 100% cotton (125 m / 50 g)
yarn_weight_class   <- "Sport (#2) 100% Mercerized/Combed Cotton"
skein_meters        <- 125.0
skein_grams         <- 50.0
meters_per_gram     <- skein_meters / skein_grams
yardage_buffer      <- 1.15  # +15% safety buffer

# 4-color palette & 2-row stripe sequence (C2 -> C3 -> C4 -> C1)
palette_df <- tibble::tibble(
  code = c("C1", "C2", "C3", "C4"),
  name = c("Forest Green", "Ochre / Mustard", "Cream", "Dusty Rose"),
  hex  = c("#2E5A36", "#B87B28", "#F3EAD6", "#D99B96"),
  role = c(
    "Body stripe 4 + Ribbed band + Cutout border + I-cord straps",
    "Body stripe 1 + Final collar/armhole sc framing row",
    "Body stripe 2",
    "Body stripe 3"
  )
)
stripe_cycle_codes <- c("C2", "C3", "C4", "C1")
rows_per_stripe    <- 2L

# Hooks (mm)
hook_body_mm <- 3.0  # Main hdc mitered chevron body
hook_trim_mm <- 2.5  # sc BLO ribbed band, inner cutout border & 3-st I-cords

# Main body gauge (3.0 mm hook in hdc): 22 sts x 16 rows = 10 x 10 cm
sts_per_cm  <- 2.2
rows_per_cm <- 1.6

# Ribbed band & trim gauge (2.5 mm hook in sc BLO): 24 sts x 26 rows = 10 x 10 cm
band_sts_per_cm  <- 2.4
band_rows_per_cm <- 2.6

# Target garment geometry (cm) -- calibrated for Size S/M (~76 cm underbust / ~88 cm bust)
# Cutout tuning guide: 4.5 = modest sternum | 9.0 = deep keyhole | 11.0 = almost-underboob | 12.5 = bold underboob
front_width_cm       <- 38.0  # Total flat horizontal baseline across front ribs
cutout_height_cm     <- 11.0  # 90-deg almost-underboob inverted-V cutout (base = 2 * 11.0 = 22.0 cm)
body_height_cm       <- 21.0  # Top of waistband (y = 0) to flat halter collarbone edge
neck_flat_width_cm   <- 9.0   # Blunted horizontal top collar width
band_height_cm       <- 4.5   # Perpendicular sc BLO underbust band height
band_total_length_cm <- 66.0  # 38 cm front (incl. 22 cm cutout bridge) + 2 x 14 cm back
back_gap_cm          <- 10.0  # Open corset lace-up gap at center back (66 + 10 = 76 cm)
icord_length_cm      <- 160.0 # Length of each 3-stitch I-cord strap (x2 straps)
icord_stitches       <- 3L



Exact Mitered Trigonometric Engine
Because hdc stitches are narrower than they are tall (1 / sts_per_cm = 0.455 cm wide vs. dT = 1 / rows_per_cm = 0.625 cm perpendicular row thickness), naive +1 or +2 increases every row distort the 90° chevron angle:

Perpendicular row thickness: \(dT = 1 / \text{rows\_per\_cm}\). Along a \(45^\circ\) chevron leg, advancing perpendicular to the leg by \(dT\) shifts the vertical spine peak upward by \(\Delta y_{\text{spine}} = dT\sqrt{2}\) and shifts a horizontal \(180^\circ\) rib baseline outward by \(\Delta x_{\text{rib}} = dT\sqrt{2}\).
90° Center Peak & 180° Rib Baseline Rate: Projecting the new vertex back onto the previous \(45^\circ\) leg yields an exact leg extension of \(dT / \tan(45^\circ) = dT\) cm per row at the spine (and likewise \(+dT\) cm per row at the flat horizontal rib edge), requiring: \[r_{\text{miter}} = dT \times \text{sts\_per\_cm} = \frac{\text{sts\_per\_cm}}{\text{rows\_per\_cm}} = 1.375 \text{ sts/row/wing}\] Our engine tracks exact cumulative Euclidean arc length with staggered tie-breaking between +1 ((1 hdc, ch 1, 1 hdc)) and +2 ((2 hdc, ch 1, 2 hdc)) so stitch counts never drift by more than 0.5 stitches (~2 mm) on any row.
Armhole Side-Bust Pivot Condition: Decreasing k stitches at the row end shortens the leg by \(s = k / \text{sts\_per\_cm}\), shifting the outer coordinate by \(\Delta x = (dT - s)/\sqrt{2}\) and \(\Delta y = (dT + s)/\sqrt{2}\). A single hdc2tog (k = 1, \(s = 0.455\text{ cm} < dT = 0.625\text{ cm}\)) actually drifts outward (\(\Delta x = +0.12\text{ cm/row}\)). To pivot strictly upward and inward (\(\Delta x < 0\)), the engine computes \(k_{\text{dec}} = \lfloor r_{\text{miter}} \rfloor + 1 = 2\) ([hdc2tog] 2x at outer edges, giving \(\Delta x = -0.20\text{ cm/row}, \Delta y = +1.08\text{ cm/row}\)).



Show R setup & trigonometric stitch engine
build_chevron_halter <- function(
  sts_per_cm, rows_per_cm, band_sts_per_cm, band_rows_per_cm,
  front_width_cm, cutout_height_cm, body_height_cm, neck_flat_width_cm,
  band_height_cm, band_total_length_cm, icord_length_cm,
  palette_df, stripe_cycle_codes, rows_per_stripe = 2L
) {
  # Fundamental differential geometry constants
  dT         <- 1 / rows_per_cm
  ds         <- 1 / sts_per_cm
  step_c     <- dT * sqrt(2)            # Intercept advance along x + y = c per hdc row
  rate_miter <- dT * sts_per_cm         # Exact sts/row/wing for 90-deg miter & 180-deg base

  # Cutout & Phase 1 foundation geometry
  cutout_base_cm <- 2 * cutout_height_cm
  cutout_leg_cm  <- cutout_height_cm * sqrt(2)
  leg0_sts       <- as.integer(round(cutout_leg_cm * sts_per_cm))
  fsc_total_sts  <- 2L * leg0_sts + 1L  # Odd count: leg + 1 marked center st + leg

  # Row milestones across phases
  rib_wing_target_cm <- (front_width_cm - cutout_base_cm) / 2
  n_rib_rows  <- as.integer(round(rib_wing_target_cm / step_c))
  n_peak_rows <- as.integer(round((body_height_cm - cutout_height_cm) / step_c))
  n_neck_rows <- as.integer(round((neck_flat_width_cm / 2) / step_c))
  n_hdc_rows  <- n_peak_rows + n_neck_rows

  # Minimum outer-edge decrease so dx = (dT - k*ds)/sqrt(2) < 0 (strictly inward taper)
  dec_outer_sts <- as.integer(floor(rate_miter) + 1L)

  color_lookup <- setNames(
    paste0(palette_df$code, " (", palette_df$name, ")"),
    palette_df$code
  )
  hex_lookup <- setNames(palette_df$hex, palette_df$code)

  # Initialize state trackers
  rows_list      <- list()
  poly_list      <- list()
  wing_sts       <- leg0_sts
  cum_peak_exact <- 0.0; cum_peak_int <- 0L
  cum_rib_exact  <- 0.0; cum_rib_int  <- 0L
  cum_neck_exact <- 0.0; cum_neck_int <- 0L

  # Row 0: Phase 1 Foundation Arch (fsc framing cutout in C2 so first stripe begins cleanly)
  first_code <- stripe_cycle_codes[1]
  rows_list[[1]] <- tibble::tibble(
    Row              = "Row 0 (Fdn)",
    row_num          = 0L,
    Phase            = "Phase 1: Foundation Arch",
    color_code       = first_code,
    Color            = color_lookup[[first_code]],
    Row_Start_Action = paste0("fsc ", leg0_sts, " (right leg)"),
    Center_Action    = "1 fsc (mark center spine st)",
    Row_End_Action   = paste0("fsc ", leg0_sts, " (left leg)"),
    Wing_Sts         = leg0_sts,
    Total_Sts        = fsc_total_sts,
    Active_HDC_Equiv = fsc_total_sts
  )

  # Physical coordinate state for right-half polygons (mirrored to left half x -> -x)
  y_collar_actual <- cutout_height_cm + n_peak_rows * step_c
  x_out_bot       <- cutout_height_cm
  y_out_bot       <- 0.0

  for (r in seq_len(n_hdc_rows)) {
    c_code <- stripe_cycle_codes[((r - 1L) %/% rows_per_stripe) %% length(stripe_cycle_codes) + 1L]
    c_bot  <- cutout_height_cm + (r - 1L) * step_c
    c_top  <- cutout_height_cm + r * step_c

    if (r <= n_rib_rows) {
      phase_label <- "Phase 2: Rib Baseline"
      # Staggered rounding tie-breakers keep wing_sts within <= 0.5 st of exact Euclidean length
      cum_peak_exact <- cum_peak_exact + rate_miter
      inc_peak       <- as.integer(floor(cum_peak_exact + 0.5)) - cum_peak_int
      cum_peak_int   <- cum_peak_int + inc_peak

      cum_rib_exact  <- cum_rib_exact + rate_miter
      inc_rib        <- as.integer(ceiling(cum_rib_exact - 0.5)) - cum_rib_int
      cum_rib_int    <- cum_rib_int + inc_rib

      wing_sts  <- wing_sts + inc_rib + inc_peak
      total_sts <- 2L * wing_sts + 1L

      start_act <- sprintf("+%d st (%d hdc in 1st st)", inc_rib, inc_rib + 1L)
      peak_act  <- sprintf("(%d hdc, ch 1, %d hdc) [+%d/wing]", inc_peak, inc_peak, inc_peak)
      end_act   <- sprintf("+%d st (%d hdc in last st)", inc_rib, inc_rib + 1L)

      x_in_bot <- 0.0;   y_in_bot <- c_bot
      x_in_top <- 0.0;   y_in_top <- c_top
      x_out_top <- c_top; y_out_top <- 0.0

    } else if (r <= n_peak_rows) {
      phase_label <- "Phase 3: Armhole Taper"
      cum_peak_exact <- cum_peak_exact + rate_miter
      inc_peak       <- as.integer(floor(cum_peak_exact + 0.5)) - cum_peak_int
      cum_peak_int   <- cum_peak_int + inc_peak

      wing_sts  <- wing_sts - dec_outer_sts + inc_peak
      total_sts <- 2L * wing_sts + 1L

      start_act <- sprintf("-%d sts ([hdc2tog] x%d)", dec_outer_sts, dec_outer_sts)
      peak_act  <- sprintf("(%d hdc, ch 1, %d hdc) [+%d/wing]", inc_peak, inc_peak, inc_peak)
      end_act   <- sprintf("-%d sts ([hdc2tog] x%d)", dec_outer_sts, dec_outer_sts)

      x_in_bot  <- 0.0; y_in_bot <- c_bot
      x_in_top  <- 0.0; y_in_top <- c_top
      x_out_top <- x_out_bot + (dT - dec_outer_sts * ds) / sqrt(2)
      y_out_top <- c_top - x_out_top

    } else {
      phase_label <- "Phase 4: Neck Short Rows"
      sr_idx      <- r - n_peak_rows
      cum_neck_exact <- cum_neck_exact + rate_miter
      dec_neck       <- as.integer(floor(cum_neck_exact + 0.5)) - cum_neck_int
      cum_neck_int   <- cum_neck_int + dec_neck

      wing_sts  <- wing_sts - dec_outer_sts - dec_neck
      total_sts <- 2L * wing_sts  # Worked separately on Left & Right shoulders

      if (sr_idx %% 2L == 1L) {
        # Odd short row: work from outer armhole edge up toward collarbone, stop short
        start_act <- sprintf("Outer: [hdc2tog] x%d (-%d sts)", dec_outer_sts, dec_outer_sts)
        peak_act  <- sprintf("Turn %d st(s) before neck edge", dec_neck)
        end_act   <- "Repeat symm. on 2nd shoulder"
      } else {
        # Even short row: sl st down along flat collar, work down to outer armhole decrease
        start_act <- sprintf("Neck: sl st %d, ch 1 (-%d sts)", dec_neck, dec_neck)
        peak_act  <- "Center unworked (flat collar)"
        end_act   <- sprintf("Outer: [hdc2tog] x%d (-%d sts)", dec_outer_sts, dec_outer_sts)
      }

      x_in_bot  <- c_bot - y_collar_actual; y_in_bot <- y_collar_actual
      x_in_top  <- c_top - y_collar_actual; y_in_top <- y_collar_actual
      x_out_top <- x_out_bot + (dT - dec_outer_sts * ds) / sqrt(2)
      y_out_top <- c_top - x_out_top
    }

    rows_list[[r + 1L]] <- tibble::tibble(
      Row              = paste0("Row ", r),
      row_num          = r,
      Phase            = phase_label,
      color_code       = c_code,
      Color            = color_lookup[[c_code]],
      Row_Start_Action = start_act,
      Center_Action    = peak_act,
      Row_End_Action   = end_act,
      Wing_Sts         = wing_sts,
      Total_Sts        = total_sts,
      Active_HDC_Equiv = total_sts
    )

    # Store right and mirrored left wing polygons for ggplot2 blueprints
    poly_list[[2L * r - 1L]] <- tibble::tibble(
      row_num = r, side = "Right", poly_id = paste0("R_", r),
      Phase = phase_label, color_code = c_code, hex = hex_lookup[[c_code]],
      x = c(x_in_bot, x_out_bot, x_out_top, x_in_top),
      y = c(y_in_bot, y_out_bot, y_out_top, y_in_top)
    )
    poly_list[[2L * r]] <- tibble::tibble(
      row_num = r, side = "Left", poly_id = paste0("L_", r),
      Phase = phase_label, color_code = c_code, hex = hex_lookup[[c_code]],
      x = -c(x_in_bot, x_out_bot, x_out_top, x_in_top),
      y =  c(y_in_bot, y_out_bot, y_out_top, y_in_top)
    )

    x_out_bot <- x_out_top
    y_out_bot <- y_out_top
  }

  # Final Framing Row: 1 continuous row of C2 (Ochre) sc framing both armholes + neckline
  side_bust_len_cm  <- sqrt((x_out_bot - (cutout_height_cm + n_rib_rows * step_c))^2 + y_out_bot^2)
  diag_arm_len_cm   <- sqrt((x_out_bot - (c_top - y_collar_actual))^2 + (y_collar_actual - y_out_bot)^2)
  collar_actual_cm  <- 2 * (c_top - y_collar_actual)
  armhole_sc_per_sd <- as.integer(round((side_bust_len_cm + diag_arm_len_cm) * sts_per_cm))
  collar_sc_sts     <- as.integer(round(collar_actual_cm * sts_per_cm))
  trim_total_sc     <- 2L * armhole_sc_per_sd + collar_sc_sts

  rows_list[[n_hdc_rows + 2L]] <- tibble::tibble(
    Row              = paste0("Row ", n_hdc_rows + 1L, " (Trim)"),
    row_num          = n_hdc_rows + 1L,
    Phase            = "Phase 4: Collar & Armhole Edging",
    color_code       = "C2",
    Color            = color_lookup[["C2"]],
    Row_Start_Action = paste0("RS join at R underarm: ", armhole_sc_per_sd, " sc up R armhole"),
    Center_Action    = paste0(collar_sc_sts, " sc across flat horizontal neckline"),
    Row_End_Action   = paste0(armhole_sc_per_sd, " sc down L armhole"),
    Wing_Sts         = armhole_sc_per_sd,
    Total_Sts        = trim_total_sc,
    Active_HDC_Equiv = as.integer(round(trim_total_sc * 0.75))
  )

  # Perpendicular sc BLO Ribbed Waistband & Cutout Stabilization Calculations (2.5 mm hook, C1)
  band_width_sts    <- as.integer(round(band_height_cm * band_sts_per_cm))
  back_ext_cm       <- (band_total_length_cm - front_width_cm) / 2
  rows_back_ext     <- 2L * as.integer(round((back_ext_cm * band_rows_per_cm) / 2))
  rows_front_wing   <- 2L * as.integer(round((rib_wing_target_cm * band_rows_per_cm) / 2))
  rows_cutout_brdg  <- 2L * as.integer(round((cutout_base_cm * band_rows_per_cm) / 2))
  band_total_rows   <- 2L * rows_back_ext + 2L * rows_front_wing + rows_cutout_brdg

  cutout_leg_sc     <- as.integer(round(cutout_leg_cm * band_sts_per_cm))
  cutout_base_sc    <- as.integer(round(cutout_base_cm * band_sts_per_cm))
  cutout_round_sts  <- 2L * (cutout_leg_sc - 1L) + 1L + cutout_base_sc # incl. sc3tog apex

  icord_rows_each   <- as.integer(round(icord_length_cm * band_rows_per_cm))

  list(
    rows_df           = bind_rows(rows_list),
    polys_df          = bind_rows(poly_list),
    dT                = dT,
    step_c            = step_c,
    rate_miter        = rate_miter,
    leg0_sts          = leg0_sts,
    fsc_total_sts     = fsc_total_sts,
    n_rib_rows        = n_rib_rows,
    n_peak_rows       = n_peak_rows,
    n_neck_rows       = n_neck_rows,
    n_hdc_rows        = n_hdc_rows,
    dec_outer_sts     = dec_outer_sts,
    front_actual_cm   = 2 * (cutout_height_cm + n_rib_rows * step_c),
    y_collar_actual   = y_collar_actual,
    collar_actual_cm  = collar_actual_cm,
    x_underarm_top    = x_out_bot,
    y_underarm_top    = y_out_bot,
    armhole_sc_per_sd = armhole_sc_per_sd,
    collar_sc_sts     = collar_sc_sts,
    band_width_sts    = band_width_sts,
    back_ext_cm       = back_ext_cm,
    rows_back_ext     = rows_back_ext,
    rows_front_wing   = rows_front_wing,
    rows_cutout_brdg  = rows_cutout_brdg,
    band_total_rows   = band_total_rows,
    cutout_leg_sc     = cutout_leg_sc,
    cutout_base_sc    = cutout_base_sc,
    cutout_round_sts  = cutout_round_sts,
    icord_rows_each   = icord_rows_each
  )
}

pat <- build_chevron_halter(
  sts_per_cm = sts_per_cm, rows_per_cm = rows_per_cm,
  band_sts_per_cm = band_sts_per_cm, band_rows_per_cm = band_rows_per_cm,
  front_width_cm = front_width_cm, cutout_height_cm = cutout_height_cm,
  body_height_cm = body_height_cm, neck_flat_width_cm = neck_flat_width_cm,
  band_height_cm = band_height_cm, band_total_length_cm = band_total_length_cm,
  icord_length_cm = icord_length_cm, palette_df = palette_df,
  stripe_cycle_codes = stripe_cycle_codes, rows_per_stripe = rows_per_stripe
)

text:
2. Visual Schematics

Figure 1: True-to-Scale Garment Blueprint & 2-Row Stripe Map


Show R setup & trigonometric stitch engine
half_band   <- band_total_length_cm / 2
half_front  <- pat$front_actual_cm / 2
half_collar <- pat$collar_actual_cm / 2
y_col       <- pat$y_collar_actual

# Anatomical S/M bust contour & apex reference (~88 cm bust: r = 7.5 cm mounds resting on y = 0 at x = +-10 cm)
theta_seq <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 180)
bust_contours <- bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(side = "L", x = -10.0 + 7.5 * cos(theta_seq), y = 7.5 + 7.5 * sin(theta_seq)),
  tibble::tibble(side = "R", x =  10.0 + 7.5 * cos(theta_seq), y = 7.5 + 7.5 * sin(theta_seq))
)
bust_apex_pts <- tibble::tibble(x = c(-10.2, 10.2), y = c(8.2, 8.2))

# Ribbed band polygon & vertical rib texture lines
band_rect <- tibble::tibble(
  xmin = -half_band, xmax = half_band,
  ymin = -band_height_cm, ymax = 0
)
rib_lines <- tibble::tibble(
  x = seq(-half_band + 0.75, half_band - 0.75, by = 0.75)
)

# Buttonhole eyelets at both back ends (3 eyelets per side)
eyelet_y <- seq(-band_height_cm * 0.78, -band_height_cm * 0.22, length.out = 3)
eyelets_df <- bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(x = -half_band + 1.1, y = eyelet_y),
  tibble::tibble(x =  half_band - 1.1, y = eyelet_y)
)

# Ochre (C2) continuous sc trim path along armholes + flat collar
ochre_trim_path <- tibble::tibble(
  x = c(half_front, pat$x_underarm_top, half_collar, -half_collar, -pat$x_underarm_top, -half_front),
  y = c(0, pat$y_underarm_top, y_col, y_col, pat$y_underarm_top, 0)
)

# Inner cutout C1 sc stabilization border triangle
cutout_border_path <- tibble::tibble(
  x = c(-cutout_height_cm, 0, cutout_height_cm, -cutout_height_cm),
  y = c(0, cutout_height_cm, 0, 0)
)

# Short I-cord strap stubs indicating strap emergence at collar corners
strap_stubs <- bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(side = "L", x = c(-half_collar, -half_collar - 1.8), y = c(y_col, y_col + 3.4)),
  tibble::tibble(side = "R", x = c( half_collar,  half_collar + 1.8), y = c(y_col, y_col + 3.4))
)

ggplot() +
  # 1. Forest Green perpendicular sc BLO ribbed band
  geom_rect(
    data = band_rect,
    aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax),
    fill = "#2E5A36", color = "#1B3821", linewidth = 0.6
  ) +
  geom_segment(
    data = rib_lines,
    aes(x = x, xend = x, y = -band_height_cm, yend = 0),
    color = "#3E7448", linewidth = 0.25, alpha = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = eyelets_df, aes(x = x, y = y),
    shape = 21, size = 2.4, fill = "#FAF8F2", color = "#1B3821", stroke = 0.7
  ) +

  # 2. Mitered chevron & short-row polygons (true 2-row stripe colors)
  geom_polygon(
    data = pat$polys_df,
    aes(x = x, y = y, group = poly_id, fill = color_code),
    color = "#2B2B2B33", linewidth = 0.2
  ) +
  # Subtle anatomical S/M bust mound & apex reference showing almost-underboob reveal vs safe apex coverage
  geom_path(
    data = bust_contours, aes(x = x, y = y, group = side),
    color = "#5C3A3866", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.45
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = bust_apex_pts, aes(x = x, y = y),
    shape = 4, size = 2.0, stroke = 0.7, color = "#5C3A3888"
  ) +
  # Highlight center mitered spine (Rows 1..n_peak_rows)
  annotate(
    "segment", x = 0, xend = 0, y = cutout_height_cm, yend = y_col,
    color = "#2B2B2B88", linetype = "dotted", linewidth = 0.5
  ) +

  # 3. Inner cutout C1 sc + surface sl st stabilization trim
  geom_path(
    data = cutout_border_path, aes(x = x, y = y),
    color = "#2E5A36", linewidth = 1.5, lineend = "round", linejoin = "mitre"
  ) +

  # 4. Ochre (C2) continuous sc edging framing both armholes & flat neckline
  geom_path(
    data = ochre_trim_path, aes(x = x, y = y),
    color = "#B87B28", linewidth = 1.8, lineend = "round", linejoin = "round"
  ) +

Yarn consumption is derived directly from stitch geometry: each 3.0 mm hdc consumes yarn proportional to its stitch footprint \((1/\text{sts\_per\_cm} + 1/\text{rows\_per\_cm})\), while 2.5 mm sc BLO ribbing, the inner cutout stabilization border, and both 160 cm 3-stitch I-cord straps are summed and multiplied by the +15% buffer.

# Physics-based yarn length per stitch calibrated to #2 Sport cotton
m_per_hdc   <- 0.0225 * ((1 / sts_per_cm + 1 / rows_per_cm) / (1 / 2.2 + 1 / 1.6))
m_per_fsc   <- 0.88 * m_per_hdc
m_per_sc30  <- 0.72 * m_per_hdc
m_per_sc25  <- 0.0175 * ((1 / band_sts_per_cm + 1 / band_rows_per_cm) / (1 / 2.4 + 1 / 2.6))
m_per_sl25  <- 0.62 * m_per_sc25

# Body yarn by color code
body_yarn <- pat$rows_df %>%
  mutate(
    raw_meters = case_when(
      row_num == 0L ~ Total_Sts * m_per_fsc,
      row_num == pat$n_hdc_rows + 1L ~ Total_Sts * m_per_sc30,
      TRUE ~ Total_Sts * m_per_hdc
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(color_code) %>%
  summarise(
    Body_Stitches = sum(Total_Sts),
    Body_Meters   = sum(raw_meters),
    .groups       = "drop"
  )

cutout_meters <- pat$cutout_round_sts * (m_per_sc25 + m_per_sl25)

section: 5. Abbreviations & Cotton Structural Notes (US Crochet Terms)
text:
5. Abbreviations & Cotton Structural Notes (US Crochet Terms)

Ch — Chain
Sl St — Slip stitch
SC — Single crochet
SC BLO — Single crochet worked in the back loop only (creates elastic vertical knit-look ribbing when turned perpendicular)
FSC — Foundation single crochet (creates chain + first sc row simultaneously with matching stretch)
HDC — Half double crochet
HDC2Tog — Half double crochet 2 stitches together ([hdc2tog] x2 works two consecutive decreases over 4 stitches, decreasing by 2 stitches)
SC3Tog — Single crochet 3 stitches together (mitered inner-corner decrease at cutout apex)
JAYG — Join-as-you-go slip-stitch attachment


Structural Anti-Sag Engineering for 100% Cotton

Zero-Bulk Stripe Transitions (Crocheting Over Tails): Because every stripe is exactly 2 rows (C2 -> C3 -> C4 -> C1), all color joins up to Row 11 land at the same right-hand edge. Change colors on the final yarn-over pull-through of the second row in each stripe, leave a 10 cm tail, and crochet directly over both the old and new yarn tails for the first 6–8 sts of the next row. In inelastic 100% cotton, locking tails inside the outer edge reinforces the rib baseline and armhole selvedges while eliminating weaving-in bulk.
Preventing Sternum Cutout Bridge Dip: Across the 22.0 cm empty sternum cutout, the Forest Green (C1) ribbed band bridges open air without upper fabric pulling it upward. Switching down to the 2.5 mm hook and working 1 snug round of sc (sc3tog at the apex) + 1 round of surface sl st around the interior perimeter of the cutout triangle locks the 45° bias edges and anchors the bridged band horizontally so it never sags or gapes on the body.
Why Outer Armholes Use [hdc2tog] x2: At 2.2 sts/cm and 1.6 rows/cm, one hdc row is 0.625 cm thick whereas one hdc stitch is only 0.455 cm wide. A single hdc2tog (-1 st) fails to overcome the outward \(45^\circ\) row projection. Working [hdc2tog] x2 (-2 sts at each outer edge) cleanly pivots the side-bust inward toward the collarbone.

text:
7. Step-by-Step Written Instructions

Phase 1 — Foundation Arch (Row 0, 3.0 mm hook)

With C2 (Ochre) and the 3.0 mm hook, work 69 fsc.
Place a locking stitch marker in the 35th (center) stitch (34 sts on Right Wing + 1 center spine st + 34 sts on Left Wing). Turn. (Note: Row 0 establishes the flexible 15.56 cm-per-leg cutout foundation rim; Rows 1–2 begin the 2-row stripe count in C2.)



Phase 2 — Flat Rib Baseline Expansion (Rows 1–9, 3.0 mm hook)
Work back and forth in 2-row stripes following the color rotation C2 -> C3 -> C4 -> C1, changing colors at the right-hand edge after every even-numbered row and crocheting over yarn tails for 6–8 sts:

Row 1 (RS, C2): Ch 1 (does not count as a st throughout), follow the Row Start Action in the first fsc (2 hdc for +1 inc, or 3 hdc for +2 inc), hdc in each remaining fsc up to the marked center stitch, work the Center Peak Action — either (1 hdc, ch 1, 1 hdc) or (2 hdc, ch 1, 2 hdc) as listed in the table — directly into the marked center fsc (move marker to the new ch-1 space), hdc down the second wing to the last st, and work the Row End Action in the last st. Turn. (36 sts per wing; 73 sts total incl. ch-1 sp).
Rows 2–9: Ch 1, work the listed Row Start Action (2 hdc or 3 hdc in first st), hdc in each st to the center ch-1 space, work the listed Center Peak Action into the ch-1 space, hdc in each st to the last st, and work the listed Row End Action in the final st. Turn.
After Row 9 (C2 (Ochre / Mustard)), your flat 180° bottom rib edge measures 37.9 cm (8.0 cm left wing + 22.0 cm almost-underboob center cutout + 8.0 cm right wing) with 58 sts per wing. Place markers at both outer bottom underarm/rib corners.



Phase 3 — Armhole Side-Bust Taper (Rows 10–11, 3.0 mm hook)
Continue the 2-row stripe sequence, maintaining the center ch-1 spine increases while switching outer row ends to double decreases so the sides pivot upward and inward along the side-bust:

Rows 10–11: Ch 1, [hdc2tog] x2 over the first 4 sts (-2 sts), hdc in each st to the center ch-1 space, work the listed Center Peak Action in the ch-1 space, hdc in each st until 4 sts remain, [hdc2tog] x2 over the last 4 sts (-2 sts). Turn.
At the end of Row 11 (C3 (Cream)), the center spine peak reaches 20.7 cm (`~21.0 cm target, 57 sts per wing). Position yarn at the outer armhole edge for the first shoulder’s short rows.



Phase 4 — Short-Row Blunted Neckline & Ochre Framing Row (Rows 12–16 + Trim)
Work each shoulder separately across 5 short rows to level off a crisp 9.0 cm horizontal collarbone edge:

First Shoulder (Rows 12–16):

Odd Short Rows (Rows 12, 14, 16 — worked Outer Armhole \(\to\) Neck): Ch 1, [hdc2tog] x2 over first 4 sts, hdc up the wing stopping 1 or 2 sts short of the previous row’s neck end as specified in the table. Leave remaining neck st(s) unworked. Turn.
Even Short Rows (Rows 13, 15 — worked Neck \(\to\) Outer Armhole): Do not ch 1; sl st loosely across the first 1 or 2 neck sts as listed in the table, ch 1, hdc in next st and down the wing until 4 sts remain, [hdc2tog] x2 over last 4 sts. Change color at the outer armhole edge after every 2-row stripe. Fasten off after Row 16 (C1 (Forest Green), 40 live diagonal armhole sts remaining).

Second Shoulder (Rows 12–16): Join C3 (Cream) at the opposite outer armhole edge and mirror Rows 12–16 identically. Fasten off.
Collar & Armhole Framing Row (Row 17, C2 Ochre, 3.0 mm hook): With RS facing, join C2 (Ochre) at the right bottom underarm marker. Ch 1, work 58 sc evenly up the right side-bust row ends and across the 40 live diagonal shoulder stitches to the right collarbone corner (2 sc in corner), work 19 sc evenly across the stepped short-row ends + center ch-1 peak to form a smooth 9.0 cm horizontal collar (2 sc in left collarbone corner), and work 58 sc down the left live diagonal shoulder stitches and left side-bust row ends to the left underarm marker. Fasten off C2.



Phase 5 — Join-As-You-Go Perpendicular sc BLO Band & Cutout Stabilization (2.5 mm hook, C1)


Show R setup & trigonometric stitch engine
# Compute symmetrical 3-eyelet buttonhole row across band_width_sts
n_eyelets   <- 3L
eyelet_ch   <- 1L
rem_sc      <- pat$band_width_sts - n_eyelets * eyelet_ch
seg_base    <- rem_sc %/% (n_eyelets + 1L)
seg_extra   <- rem_sc %%  (n_eyelets + 1L)
seg_vec     <- rep(seg_base, n_eyelets + 1L)
if (seg_extra > 0) seg_vec[seq_len(seg_extra)] <- seg_vec[seq_len(seg_extra)] + 1L
eyelet_instr <- paste0(
  "sc BLO ", seg_vec[1], ", ",
  paste(sprintf("[ch %d, sk %d, sc BLO %d]", eyelet_ch, eyelet_ch, seg_vec[-1]), collapse = ", ")
)


Switch to the 2.5 mm hook and C1 (Forest Green). The 4.5 cm band is worked perpendicular to the body (11 sts wide \(\times\) 170 rows = 66.0 cm):

Left Back Extension (Band Rows 1–36, 14.0 cm):

Ch 12. Row 1: sc in 2nd ch from hook and each ch across (11 sts). Ch 1, turn.
Row 2 (Left Corset Buttonhole Row): Work 3 evenly spaced lacing eyelets: sc BLO 2, [ch 1, sk 1, sc BLO 2], [ch 1, sk 1, sc BLO 2], [ch 1, sk 1, sc BLO 2] (11 sts incl. ch-1 spaces). Ch 1, turn.
Rows 3–36: sc BLO in each st (and into each ch-1 eyelet on Row 3) across (11 sts), ch 1, turn at the outer edge. At the top edge of Row 36, align with the left bottom underarm marker on the RS of the body.

Left Front Rib Wing — JAYG (Band Rows 37–56, 8.0 cm):

At the body edge after every odd band row, sl st into the next two 2.4 sts/cm-spaced edge points along the horizontal bottom rib baseline of Phase 2 (sl st 1 to join, sl st 1 to advance, turn — do not ch 1 at the body edge), then sc BLO 11 down to the bottom hem, ch 1, turn, and sc BLO 11 back up to the body. Stop precisely at the left base corner of the inverted-V cutout.

Sternum Cutout Bridge (Band Rows 57–114, 22.0 cm):

Work 58 rows of sc BLO (11 sts, ch 1, turn at both top and bottom edges) unattached across open air to bridge the 22.0 cm base of the sternum cutout. Keep tension firm so the bridge matches 22.0 cm unstretched.

Right Front Rib Wing — JAYG (Band Rows 115–134, 8.0 cm):

Resume sl st join-as-you-go attachment starting at the right base corner of the inverted-V cutout all the way out to the right bottom underarm marker.

Right Back Extension & Right Eyelets (Band Rows 135–170, 14.0 cm):

Continue sc BLO unattached for 34 rows.
Row 169 (Right Corset Buttonhole Row): Work sc BLO 2, [ch 1, sk 1, sc BLO 2], [ch 1, sk 1, sc BLO 2], [ch 1, sk 1, sc BLO 2] to mirror the 3 left eyelets.
Row 170: sc BLO in each st/ch across (11 sts). Fasten off.

Inner Cutout Anti-Sag Stabilization Round (2.5 mm hook, C1):

With RS facing, join C1 at the right bottom corner inside the cutout triangle. Work 36 sc evenly up the underside of the right foundation arch leg, work sc3tog across (last st before apex, center spine st, first st down left leg) to lock a crisp 90° apex, work 36 sc down the left leg, and work 53 sc across the top row-ends of the bridged band (126 sts), sl st to join.
Work 1 round of firm surface sl st around all 126 sts of the cutout triangle. Fasten off and weave in ends securely.




Phase 6 — 3-Stitch I-Cord Straps & Wet-Blocking (2.5 mm hook, C1)

Right & Left 3-Stitch I-Cords (2 x 160 cm):

With C1 (Forest Green) and the 2.5 mm hook, insert hook into the right collarbone corner of the Ochre collar trim and pull up 3 loops across the 2 corner stitches (3 loops on hook).
I-Cord Repeat (~416 rows): Drop the 2nd and 3rd loops from the hook (pinch firmly with left thumb and forefinger so they do not unravel), yo and pull through 1st loop; insert hook into 2nd loop, yo and pull through; insert hook into 3rd loop, yo and pull through (3 live loops restored). Repeat until cord measures 160 cm, then yo and pull through all 3 loops at once. Fasten off.
Repeat identically at the left collarbone corner.

Wet-Blocking Dimensions & Corset Lacing:

Soak the finished cotton halter in cool water with mild no-rinse wash for 15 minutes; gently squeeze in a towel without wringing.
Pin flat to a blocking mat to exact target geometry:

Total Ribbed Band: 66.0 cm \(\times\) 4.5 cm (straight bottom edge, zero dip across the 22.0 cm cutout bridge).
Inverted-V Cutout: 22.0 cm base \(\times\) 11.0 cm apex height (90° inner peak).
Front Rib Baseline: 38.0 cm between underarm markers.
Body Height (above band to flat collar): 21.0 cm.
Blunted Collar Width: 9.0 cm.

Once completely dry, cross the two 160 cm I-cord straps in an “X” over the upper back and lace them downward through the 3 pairs of buttonhole eyelets across the 10 cm back corset gap, tying a bow at the lower back.

Written Pattern
Gauge: 2 HDC = 1 cm
Stitches Used: HDC (Half Double Crochet), Sl St (Slip Stitch), Ch (Chain)

Base Band

Row 1: Foundation HDC 92 (or Ch 93, HDC in 2nd ch from hook and each ch across). (92 sts)
Rows 2 - 4: Ch 1, turn. HDC in each st across. (92 sts)



Left Cup
Worked over the first 39 stitches of the Base Band.

Row 5: With the right side facing you, skip the first stitch. Attach yarn to the 2nd stitch of the Base Band. Ch 1, HDC in the same st and the next 36 sts. Leave the remaining stitches unworked. (37 sts)
Row 6: Turn, Sl St into the first st. Ch 1, HDC in the next 35 sts. Leave the last st unworked. (35 sts)
Rows 7 - 23: Repeat the process from Row 6 (turn, Sl St in the first st, Ch 1, HDC across leaving the last st unworked). Each row will decrease by 2 stitches (1 at the beginning, 1 at the end).
Final Row (Row 23): 1 HDC remains. Fasten off.



Right Cup
Worked over stitches 53 - 91 of the Base Band (leaving 13 stitches unworked between the cups).

Row 5: Skip 13 sts after the base of the Left Cup (sts 40-52). Attach yarn to stitch 54. Ch 1, HDC in the same st and the next 36 sts. Leave the last st (st 92) unworked. (37 sts)
Row 6: Turn, Sl St into the first st. Ch 1, HDC in the next 35 sts. Leave the last st unworked. (35 sts)
Rows 7 - 23: Repeat the process from Row 6, decreasing by 2 sts per row (skipping the first and last stitch) until 1 stitch remains. Fasten off.

text:
Written Pattern (Front Panel)
Gauge: 2 DC = 1 cm
Stitches Used: DC (Double Crochet), Ch (Chain), DC2Tog (Double Crochet 2 Together)
Note: This is worked entirely in standard Double Crochet for a classic, breathable t-shirt texture.

1. Bottom Hem

Row 1: Foundation DC 100. (Or Ch 102, DC in 3rd ch from hook and each ch across). (100 sts)
Rows 2 - 4: Ch 2, turn, DC across. (100 sts)



2. Main Body

Rows 5 - 40: Ch 2, turn, DC across. You are creating a straight tube until you reach the armpits. (100 sts)



3. Upper Chest & Armhole Shaping

Row 41: Turn, slip stitch across the first 6 sts. Ch 2, DC in the next 88 sts. Leave the last 6 sts unworked. (88 sts)
Row 42: Ch 2, turn. DC decrease (DC2Tog) across first 2 sts. DC across until last 2 sts. DC2Tog. (86 sts)
Row 43: Ch 2, turn. DC2Tog across first 2 sts. DC across until last 2 sts. DC2Tog. (84 sts)
Row 44: Ch 2, turn. DC2Tog across first 2 sts. DC across until last 2 sts. DC2Tog. (82 sts)
Row 45: Ch 2, turn. DC2Tog across first 2 sts. DC across until last 2 sts. DC2Tog. (80 sts)
Rows 46 - 51: Ch 2, turn, DC across. The armhole decrease is now complete. (80 sts)



4. Shoulders & Neckline
You will split the work to form the left and right shoulder straps.
Left Shoulder: - Row 52: With right side facing, Ch 2, DC across the first 28 sts. Leave the rest unworked. (28 sts) - Row 53: Ch 2, turn. DC2Tog at the inner neck edge. DC across remaining 26 sts. (27 sts) - Row 54: Ch 2, turn. DC across 25 sts, DC2Tog at the inner neck edge. (26 sts) - Row 55: Ch 2, turn. DC2Tog at the inner neck edge. DC across remaining 24 sts. (25 sts) - Row 56: Ch 2, turn. DC across 23 sts, DC2Tog at the inner neck edge. (24 sts) - Rows 57 - 60: Ch 2, turn, DC across. Fasten off after Row 60. (24 sts)
Right Shoulder: - Row 52: Skip the 24 center stitches of the neckline. Attach yarn to the 53rd stitch from the left armhole edge (or count 28 sts from the right armhole edge). Ch 2, DC in the 28 sts to the end. (28 sts) - Row 53: Ch 2, turn. DC across 26 sts, DC2Tog at the inner neck edge. (27 sts) - Row 54: Ch 2, turn. DC2Tog at the inner neck edge. DC across remaining 25 sts. (26 sts) - Row 55: Ch 2, turn. DC across 24 sts, DC2Tog at the inner neck edge. (25 sts) - Row 56: Ch 2, turn. DC2Tog at the inner neck edge. DC across remaining 23 sts. (24 sts) - Rows 57 - 60: Ch 2, turn, DC across. Fasten off after Row 60. (24 sts)

title: Technical Crochet Patterns
text:
Welcome to the Technical Crochet Pattern visualization repository.
Here you will find plain-text crochet measurements and stitch descriptions translated into structured R data matrices, visualized using ggplot2.

title: Crochet Vocabulary & Abbreviations
text:
Welcome to the glossary of terms used across our technical crochet patterns.

Stitches & Techniques

SC (Single Crochet)
The most basic crochet stitch, creating a tight and dense fabric. Used extensively in amigurumi to form solid, structured 3D shapes. Watch YouTube Tutorial


HDC (Half Double Crochet)
A medium-height stitch that is taller than a single crochet but shorter than a double crochet. It creates a solid, slightly textured fabric that is perfect for underboob tops and bralettes as it balances coverage and drape. Watch YouTube Tutorial


DC (Double Crochet)
A tall stitch that creates a looser, more flexible fabric compared to SC or HDC. Great for wearables like t-shirts where breathability and drape are desired. Watch YouTube Tutorial


Sl St (Slip Stitch)
A very flat, low-profile stitch. In these patterns, it is primarily used to move the yarn across the work without adding height, which creates clean, stepped decreases along armpit edges, or to finish off a round in amigurumi. Watch YouTube Tutorial


Ch (Chain)
The foundation of crochet. Chains are used to create the starting row, to add height at the beginning of a new row (a turning chain), or to bridge gaps in the fabric (like the center of a keyhole cutout or apertures in pollen grains). Watch YouTube Tutorial


Picot
A textured, decorative stitch that creates a small bump or “spike” on the fabric. In our pollen grain pattern, this is used to simulate the botanical echinae (spines). Typically made by chaining 3 and slip stitching into the first chain. Watch YouTube Tutorial


INC (Increase)
Working two stitches into the same stitch from the previous row or round. This adds to your total stitch count, expanding the width of the fabric or widening a 3D sphere. Watch YouTube Tutorial


DEC (Decrease / SC2Tog)
Combining two stitches into one. In amigurumi, this is often done using an “Invisible Decrease” to prevent gaps, effectively narrowing the 3D shape. Watch YouTube Tutorial


DC2Tog (Double Crochet 2 Together)
A decrease technique specifically for Double Crochet. It combines two stitches into one, used for shaping armholes or necklines in garments. Watch YouTube Tutorial


St / Sts (Stitch / Stitches)
The individual loops or “V” shapes along the top edge of your fabric.



Pattern Anatomy

Inner Edge / Cleavage Edge
The side of the cup that faces the center of the chest. In our patterns, this edge often features increases to curve the fabric inwards and create coverage.


Outer Edge / Armpit Edge
The side of the cup that faces your arm. This edge typically features steady decreases to taper the fabric from the base band up to the strap.

title: Pollen Grain: Succisa pratensis
text:
The Written Pattern
Hook: 3.00mm. Work in continuous spiral rounds. Use a stitch marker to track the start of each round. Note on Echinae: Wherever you see a red tile on the map above, replace the standard SC with a Picot stitch (CH 3, slip stitch into first CH).

The Monad (Base & Expansion):

R1: 6 SC in a magic ring (6)
R2: INC in each st around (12)
R3: (1 SC, INC) around (18)
R4: (2 SC, INC) around (24)
R5: (3 SC, INC) around (30)
R6: (4 SC, INC) around (36)
R7: (5 SC, INC) around (42)
R8-R11: SC around (42)



The Triporate Equator:

R12: (10 SC, Chain 4 and skip 4 stitches) x 3 times (42)
R13: SC around, placing 4 SC directly into each of the three Chain-4 gaps (42)
R14-R17: SC around (42)



Closing the Sphere:

R18: (5 SC, DEC) around (36)
R19: (4 SC, DEC) around (30)
R20: (3 SC, DEC) around (24)
(Stuff the grain firmly here. Do not overstuff the equator or the pores will bulge).
R21: (2 SC, DEC) around (18)
R22: (1 SC, DEC) around (12)
R23: DEC around (6). Fasten off.



Detailing the Apertures:

Annulus: Surface slip-stitch a raised ring tightly around the rim of each of the three R12 holes.
Operculum: Weave a loose star-shape of yarn across the center of each hole. Embroider 2 French knots in the center of the web.



How to use this outdoors:
When you push this file to your GitHub repo, Quarto will execute the R chunk, plot the specific locations of the randomized spines, and render the mobile-friendly HTML. You can just check your phone, look at the visual map for the current round, and easily spot exactly which stitches need a spike.

library(ggplot2)

# Base: 96 stitches

grid <- expand.grid(Stitch = 1:96, Row = 1:30)

grid <- grid %>%
  mutate(
    # 1. Define the physical shape of the top (reverting to the arched window look)
    Part = case_when(
      Row <= 4 ~ "Base Band",
      Row >= 5 & Row <= 12 & Stitch <= (20 + 2*(Row-5)) ~ "Lower Cup (Left)",
      Row >= 5 & Row <= 12 & Stitch >= (77 - 2*(Row-5)) ~ "Lower Cup (Right)",
      Row >= 13 & Row <= 16 & Stitch >= (1 + (Row-12)) & Stitch <= (96 - (Row-12)) ~ "Center Bridge",
      Row >= 17 & Stitch >= (5 + (Row-16)) & Stitch <= (46 - 1.5*(Row-16)) ~ "Upper Cup (Left)",
      Row >= 17 & Stitch >= (51 + 1.5*(Row-16)) & Stitch <= (92 - (Row-16)) ~ "Upper Cup (Right)",
      TRUE ~ "Empty Space"

    # 2. Define the stitch type based on location
    Stitch_Type = case_when(
      Part == "Empty Space" ~ NA_character_,
      sqrt((Stitch - 24)^2 + (Row - 18)^2) <= 8 ~ "Dense HDC (Coverage)",

  annotate("label", x = 48, y = 14.5, label = "Center Bridge\n4 rows", size = 3, fontface = "bold", fill = "#FFFFFFCC", label.size = NA) +
  annotate("label", x = 25, y = 24, label = "Left Upper Cup\n14 rows", size = 3, fontface = "bold", fill = "#FFFFFFCC", label.size = NA) +
  annotate("label", x = 71, y = 24, label = "Right Upper Cup\n14 rows", size = 3, fontface = "bold", fill = "#FFFFFFCC", label.size = NA) +

    "Base Band" = "#2C3E50",

    "Center Bridge" = "#F1C40F",
    "Upper Cup (Left)" = "#3498DB",
    "Upper Cup (Right)" = "#3498DB"

    "Standard DC (Breathable)" = 0.4,

  theme_minimal() +

title: Keyhole Underboob Top
text:
Written Pattern
Gauge: Standard DC base with dense HDC coverage zones.
Stitches Used: DC (Double Crochet), HDC (Half Double Crochet), Sl St (Slip Stitch), Ch (Chain)
Note: The pattern primarily uses Double Crochet (DC) for a breathable, looser mesh. However, around the center bust (spanning an 8-stitch radius around X=24 and X=72 on the map, roughly Rows 10-26), you will switch to Half Double Crochet (HDC) to create dense, solid coverage zones. Refer to the density map for the exact placement of HDC stitches row by row.

1. Base Band

Rows 1 - 4: Foundation DC 96. (Or Ch 98, DC in 3rd ch from hook and each ch across). For rows 2-4: Ch 2, turn, DC across. (96 sts)



2. The Cutout Region (Sides of the Window)
You will work the left and right sides separately to form the arching keyhole.
Left Side: - Row 5: With right side facing, Ch 2. DC/HDC (following the map for dense zones) in the first 20 sts. Leave the rest unworked. (20 sts) - Rows 6 - 12: Ch 2, turn. On the inner edge (the cleavage side), increase by 2 sts per row. DC/HDC in each remaining st. By Row 12, you will have grown to 34 sts. Fasten off after Row 12.
Right Side: - Row 5: Skip the next 56 sts of the Base Band (this wide gap forms the bottom of the arched keyhole window). Attach yarn to the 77th stitch. Ch 2, DC/HDC in the remaining 20 sts. (20 sts) - Rows 6 - 12: Ch 2, turn. Increase by 2 sts on the inner cleavage edge per row. DC/HDC in each remaining st. Do not fasten off; you will continue from here with 34 sts.


3. The Sternum Bridge (Closing the Window)

Row 13: (Continuing from the right side). Ch 2, turn. Skip the first st. Work across the 33 sts of the Right Side, chain 28 over the keyhole gap, and work across the 33 sts of the Left Side until 1 st remains. Leave the last st unworked. (94 sts counting the chains)
Rows 14 - 16: Ch 2, turn. Skip the first st. Work across (incorporating the chains on Row 14) following the density map, until 1 st remains. Leave the last st unworked. Each row decreases by 2 stitches (1 at each edge). By Row 16, you will have 88 sts.



4. The Upper Cups (Triangles)
You will split the work again to form the two upper triangles.
Left Upper Cup: - Row 17: With right side facing, attach yarn to the 5th st. Ch 2, work across 40 sts following the density map. (40 sts) - Rows 18 - 30: Ch 2, turn. Decrease 1 st at the armpit edge (outer edge) every row, and alternate decreasing 1 or 2 sts at the cleavage edge (inner edge) to follow the taper of the grid. Continue until Row 30. Fasten off.
Right Upper Cup: - Row 17: Attach yarn to the 52nd st. Ch 2, work across 40 sts following the density map. (40 sts) - Rows 18 - 30: Ch 2, turn. Decrease 1 st at the armpit edge, and alternate decreasing 1 or 2 sts at the cleavage edge. Continue until Row 30. Fasten off.

text:
The Written Pattern
Hook: 3.00mm with Cotton Yarn.
Note on construction: The back is left completely open. You will weave long chains through the outer edges of the side panels to lace it up your back.

Part 1: The Lower Torso

Chain 102 (100 base stitches + 2 turning chains).
Rows 1 - 20: Double Crochet (DC) across all 100 stitches. (Chain 2 to turn at the end of each row).



Part 2: The Sternum Cutout (Sides)
Here you transition to Half Double Crochet (HDC) for structure. We build the left side of the window, cut the yarn, and then build the right side.

Rows 21 - 32 (Left Side): HDC across the first 38 stitches. Chain 1 and turn. Repeat until Row 32. Fasten off.
Rows 21 - 32 (Right Side): Skip the middle 24 stitches (this is your sternum window). Attach yarn at stitch 63. HDC across the remaining 38 stitches. Chain 1 and turn. Repeat until Row 32. Fasten off.



Part 3: The Upper Chest Bridge

Row 33: Re-attach yarn at the start of the row (Stitch 1). HDC across the first 38 stitches of the left side. Chain 24 to bridge the gap. HDC across the 38 stitches of the right side. (100 total stitches/chains).
Rows 34 - 36: HDC across all 100 stitches (working directly into the 24 chains when you cross the middle).



Part 4: The Straps
These taper sharply at the armpits to create an athletic, masculine shoulder profile.

Left Strap (Rows 37 - 45): Work across the first 30 stitches. On every row, decrease (DEC) two times at the armpit edge (the outer edge, near Stitch 1). The inner edge (near Stitch 30) stays straight. Fasten off at Row 45.
Right Strap (Rows 37 - 45): Attach yarn at Stitch 71. Work to the end (Stitch 100). On every row, decrease (DEC) two times at the armpit edge (Stitch 100). The inner edge (near Stitch 71) stays straight. Fasten off at Row 45.



Finishing:
Create a 200+ chain string. Lace it up the back in an “X” corset pattern, tying it at the lower back.

text:
2. Stitch Map Visualization (Tile Grid)
Matching the geom_tile stitch-grid format of the other patterns in this repository, the front panel and bridged base band are mapped onto a discrete (Stitch, Row) matrix (1 Tile = 1 Stitch across the front panel, colored by actual yarn shade and stitch density zone), followed by an unwrapped row-by-stitch chart for counting directly off your screen.


Show R setup & trigonometric stitch engine
# Convert garment geometry into discrete front-panel stitch columns & vertical row equivalents
n_front_sts  <- 2L * as.integer(round((pat$front_actual_cm / 2) * sts_per_cm)) + 1L # odd for center spine col
center_col   <- (n_front_sts + 1L) %/% 2L
n_band_rows  <- as.integer(round(band_height_cm * rows_per_cm))
n_body_vrows <- as.integer(round(pat$y_collar_actual * rows_per_cm)) + 1L
tot_grid_rows <- n_band_rows + n_body_vrows

# Outer boundary helper at height y_cm above band
half_collar_cm <- pat$collar_actual_cm / 2
y_col_cm       <- pat$y_collar_actual
half_front_cm  <- pat$front_actual_cm / 2
x_ua_cm        <- pat$x_underarm_top
y_ua_cm        <- pat$y_underarm_top

grid <- expand.grid(
  Stitch = seq_len(n_front_sts),
  Row    = seq_len(tot_grid_rows)
) %>%
  mutate(
    # Physical coordinates (cm) of each discrete stitch tile center
    x_cm    = (Stitch - center_col) / sts_per_cm,
    y_cm    = (Row - n_band_rows - 0.5) / rows_per_cm,
    abs_x   = abs(x_cm),
    c_diag  = abs_x + y_cm,

    # Maximum outer half-width of the front body at height y_cm
    max_x_at_y = case_when(
      y_cm < 0 ~ half_front_cm,
      y_cm <= y_ua_cm ~ half_front_cm + (x_ua_cm - half_front_cm) * (y_cm / max(y_ua_cm, 0.01)),
      y_cm <= y_col_cm ~ x_ua_cm + (half_collar_cm - x_ua_cm) * ((y_cm - y_ua_cm) / max(y_col_cm - y_ua_cm, 0.01)),
      TRUE ~ -1.0
    ),

    # Chevron row index (1..n_hdc_rows) corresponding to 45-deg coordinate c_diag
    chev_row = as.integer(ceiling((c_diag - cutout_height_cm) / pat$step_c)),
    stripe_idx = ((pmax(chev_row, 1L) - 1L) %/% rows_per_stripe) %% length(stripe_cycle_codes) + 1L,
    chev_code  = stripe_cycle_codes[stripe_idx],

    # Structural region classification
    Part = case_when(
      Row <= n_band_rows ~ "Base Band (C1 sc BLO)",
      y_cm > y_col_cm ~ "Empty Space",
      abs_x > max_x_at_y ~ "Empty Space",
      c_diag < cutout_height_cm - 0.35 ~ "Empty Space",
      c_diag < cutout_height_cm + 0.28 ~ "Cutout Lock Border (C1 sc/sl st)",
      y_cm >= y_col_cm - (1 / rows_per_cm) & abs_x <= half_collar_cm + 0.35 ~ "Collar & Armhole Trim (C2 sc)",
      abs_x >= max_x_at_y - 0.48 ~ "Collar & Armhole Trim (C2 sc)",
      TRUE ~ paste0("Chevron Stripe: ", chev_code)
    ),

    # Map every active tile to its exact yarn color label
    Yarn_Shade = case_when(
      Part == "Empty Space" ~ NA_character_,
      Part %in% c("Base Band (C1 sc BLO)", "Cutout Lock Border (C1 sc/sl st)") ~ "C1: Forest Green (Band & Cutout Lock)",
      Part == "Collar & Armhole Trim (C2 sc)" ~ "C2: Ochre / Mustard (Body & Trim)",
      chev_code == "C1" ~ "C1: Forest Green (Band & Cutout Lock)",
      chev_code == "C2" ~ "C2: Ochre / Mustard (Body & Trim)",
      chev_code == "C3" ~ "C3: Cream",
      chev_code == "C4" ~ "C4: Dusty Rose"
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(Part != "Empty Space")

cutout_top_row <- n_band_rows + as.integer(round(cutout_height_cm * rows_per_cm))
ua_split_row   <- n_band_rows + as.integer(round(y_ua_cm * rows_per_cm))

  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.22) +
  # Structural phase boundary lines (matching repository pattern style)

  geom_hline(yintercept = cutout_top_row + 0.5, color = "grey45", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.5) +

  geom_vline(xintercept = center_col, color = "grey35", linetype = "dotted", linewidth = 0.5) +

    "label", x = center_col, y = (n_band_rows + 1) / 2,
    label = sprintf("Bridged Ribbed Band (%s sts front span; +2x14 cm back extensions)", n_front_sts),
    size = 3.0, fontface = "bold", fill = "#FFFFFFDD", label.size = NA
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text", x = center_col, y = n_band_rows + max(3.2, (cutout_top_row - n_band_rows) * 0.36),
    label = sprintf("Almost-Underboob\n90° Cutout Window\n(%.0f x %.0f cm)", 2 * cutout_height_cm, cutout_height_cm),

  ) +
  annotate(
    "label", x = center_col, y = cutout_top_row + round((tot_grid_rows - 5 - cutout_top_row) * 0.55),
    label = "90° Center Spine\n(+1 / +2 inc)",
    size = 2.8, fontface = "bold", fill = "#FFFFFFCC", label.size = NA
  ) +
  annotate(
    "label", x = center_col, y = tot_grid_rows - 2.2,
    label = sprintf("Short-Row Flat Collar (%.0f cm)", neck_flat_width_cm),
    size = 2.8, fontface = "bold", fill = "#FFFFFFDD", label.size = NA
  ) +

  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "C1: Forest Green (Band & Cutout Lock)" = "#2E5A36",
    "C2: Ochre / Mustard (Body & Trim)"     = "#B87B28",

  )) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +

Unwrapped Row-by-Stitch Counting Grid (Rows 0–17)
Because chevron rows run along a 45° diagonal, this companion unwrapped geom_tile matrix flattens each pattern row horizontally so 1 tile = 1 exact crochet stitch worked in that row (with special stitch actions highlighted along the outer edges and center spine).


Show R setup & trigonometric stitch engine
# Build exact stitch-by-stitch tile rows from pat$rows_df
unwrapped_tiles <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(pat$rows_df)), function(i) {
  rw    <- pat$rows_df[i, ]
  r_num <- rw$row_num
  w_sts <- rw$Wing_Sts

  if (rw$Phase == "Phase 4: Neck Short Rows") {
    # Leave visual gap in the center proportional to unworked collar stitches
    sr_step <- r_num - pat$n_peak_rows
    gap_half <- 1L + 2L * sr_step
    left_x   <- seq(-gap_half - w_sts + 1L, -gap_half)
    right_x  <- seq(gap_half, gap_half + w_sts - 1L)
    tibble::tibble(
      Row_Num    = r_num,
      Stitch_Pos = c(left_x, right_x),
      Color_Code = rw$color_code,
      Action     = case_when(
        Stitch_Pos %in% c(min(left_x), min(left_x) + 1L, max(right_x) - 1L, max(right_x)) ~ "Decrease (hdc2tog)",
        TRUE ~ "Standard Stitch"
      )
    )
  } else if (r_num == pat$n_hdc_rows + 1L) {
    # Continuous sc collar & armhole framing row
    half_tot <- rw$Total_Sts %/% 2L
    xs       <- seq(-half_tot, half_tot)
    tibble::tibble(
      Row_Num    = r_num,
      Stitch_Pos = xs,
      Color_Code = rw$color_code,
      Action     = "Standard Stitch"
    )
  } else {
    # Full mitered chevron rows (Phase 1, 2, 3): Left Wing + Center Spine (0) + Right Wing
    left_x  <- seq(-w_sts, -1L)
    right_x <- seq(1L, w_sts)
    xs      <- c(left_x, 0L, right_x)
    tibble::tibble(
      Row_Num    = r_num,
      Stitch_Pos = xs,
      Color_Code = rw$color_code,
      Action     = case_when(
        Stitch_Pos == 0L ~ "Center Spine (ch-1 / fsc)",
        rw$Phase == "Phase 3: Armhole Taper" &
          Stitch_Pos %in% c(min(left_x), min(left_x) + 1L, max(right_x) - 1L, max(right_x)) ~ "Decrease (hdc2tog)",
        rw$Phase == "Phase 2: Rib Baseline" &
          Stitch_Pos %in% c(min(left_x), max(right_x)) ~ "Increase (+1/+2)",
        TRUE ~ "Standard Stitch"
      )
    )
  }
}) %>% bind_rows()

unwrapped_markers <- unwrapped_tiles %>%
  filter(Action != "Standard Stitch")

ggplot(unwrapped_tiles, aes(x = Stitch_Pos, y = Row_Num, fill = Color_Code)) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 10.5) +
  labs(

    subtitle = "Each row flattened horizontally around Center Spine (0); center gap on Rows 12–16 shows unworked flat collar",
    x        = "Centered Stitch Index (Left Wing  <--  0  -->  Right Wing)",
